title: Deterministic temporal output after a keyframed effect-state mutation
question: Does repeating the same 120-frame evaluation preserve byte-identical output, and does changing only the midpoint Gaussian Blur keyframe alter output across the interpolated temporal interval?
source_note: Existing AE 26.3 run preserved in runs/EXP-CORE-001. CPU RIP sampling is retained but excluded from render-internal conclusions because its five-second windows ended before each render pass began.

environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER; Parsec Virtual Display Adapter
environment.notes: Environment was reconstructed from the installed AfterFX binary and raw sample module paths; see environment.txt.

hypotheses.prediction: Two evaluations of unchanged project state produce byte-identical PNG output for every sampled frame.
Changing only the middle Blur keyframe from 60 to 110 changes frames whose interpolated blur value depends on that keyframe while leaving the unchanged t=0 endpoint identical.
hypotheses.falsified_by: C remains byte-identical to B across the sequence, or frame 0 changes despite its unchanged endpoint value.

factors: Gaussian Blur middle keyframe: 60 -> 110 before pass C
three foreground layers with animated transforms and blur
procedure: Create the deterministic 512x512 five-second fixture with three animated foreground layers and Gaussian Blur keyed 5/60/5.
Evaluate all 120 frame times to PNG as pass A.
Evaluate the unchanged state again as pass B.
Change only each foreground layer's middle Blur keyframe from 60 to 110.
Evaluate all 120 frame times again as pass C and compare SHA-256 per frame.

result.conclusion: Observed: pass A and B were SHA-256 identical for all 120 frames. After changing only the midpoint Blur keyframe, pass C retained equality only at f000 and differed for f001-f119. This directly validates deterministic same-state output and temporal propagation of the keyframed state mutation across sampled interpolation times. It does not by itself identify the internal GUID or cache mechanism responsible.
result.notes: The RIP sampler does not overlap render execution: A ended 7.32 s, B 7.66 s, and C 8.16 s before the corresponding render begin timestamps. samples-A/B/C.tsv are therefore pre-render baseline captures only and are excluded from render-internal interpretation.
